title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Acme Retail
next_steps: Redwood to send POC sizing worksheet + pricing estimate (Alex) by 2025-10-17
Customer to share 3 representative workloads and sample logs (Maya) by 2025-10-20
Schedule dedicated capacity sizing deep-dive with Infra (Samir + Liam) week of 2025-10-20
Run initial latency/cost benchmark on hosted test account (Alex + Maya) by 2025-10-24
action_items: Alex Chen: Send security docs (SOC 2 summary, ISO checklist, KMS notes) - due 2025-10-17
Samir Patel: Prepare benchmark script + sample prompts for Acme workloads - due 2025-10-21

summary: POC scoping call to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Acme Retail personalization and search features. Main success criteria: latency SLOs (95th < 200ms for personalization), cost per 1k requests target, data residency and SOC2 requirements. Agreed next steps: share workloads, run hosted benchmark, and schedule dedicated sizing deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intro — Alex Chen from Redwood, i run the AE for retail. with me is Samir, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Maya (Acme): Thanks, Alex. Maya Lopez here, head of ML at Acme Retail. Liam is on infra and Jordan on product.
[00:22] Alex (AE): Great. agenda today: understand your success criteria, workloads, timelines, and then go over tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so we can scope a POC. Sound good?
[00:30] Jordan (Product): Yep, want to be pragmatic — we have a Q4 timeline to decide.
[00:36] Samir (SE): Cool. to ground the convo, can you share the two main features you want to evaluate?
[00:42] Maya (Acme): Primary is personalization - real-time recommendations for web and app. second is search re-ranking for product search. both need low lat and predictable cost.
[00:52] Liam (Infra): add constraints: must be SOC2-compliant, data residency in us-east for logs, and we use AWS with VPC peering for sensitive data.
[01:03] Alex (AE): good. success criteria — what would constitute a win for the POC?
[01:08] Maya (Acme): For personalization: 95th latency under 200ms for online calls, p50 maybe 40-60ms; for re-rank it's okay if 95th is under 400ms. Cost-wise we want to get within 30% of our internal TCO per 1k requests. And security: SOC2 + KMS integration or customer-managed keys, plus audit logs.
[01:30] Samir (SE): perfect. that gives us concrete targets. about workload sizing — what's your current traffic? qps and seq lengths?
[01:38] Liam (Infra): average qps for personalization about 80 qps, peak bursts ~350 qps during promos. median seq length is short — inputs ~30 tokens, but some user context can push to 300 tokens for session-level calls. re-rank is lower qps but larger context, avg 120 tokens.
[01:58] Samir (SE): ok that's helpful. caching and prefix caching could help with session context to save kv cache thrash.
[02:05] Jordan (Product): curious: hosted vs dedicated vs private — what are the main diffs re: latency and cost?
[02:11] Alex (AE): short answer: hosted is fastest to try and easiest to manage — we provide API, caching, model variants; good for initial bench. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full network isolation and customer-managed keys but is more ops-heavy and longer lead time.
[02:33] Maya (Acme): latency wise if we use hosted do we get 95th <200ms for personalization?
[02:39] Samir (SE): depends on model and sequence length. for small seq (<=50) we can hit sub-200ms 95th for optimized models on hosted in us-east with our streaming and kv cache. at peak concurrency we may need dedicated to keep consistent SLOs because dedicated avoids noisy neighbor effects and gives predictable burst capacity.
[02:58] Liam (Infra): cost is big — hosted per-token cost can be higher but you avoid infra ops. dedicated has commit pricing and is cheaper at sustained throughput. private has fixed infra + license and maintenance, so TCO depends on utilization.
[03:14] Jordan (Product): what about model updates and rollouts? we need A/B and canary.
[03:19] Alex (AE): supported across all modes — hosted has easiest workflow for rollouts and automatic fallback. dedicated supports canary and A/B via our runtime, you just point to different model variants; private has those features too but requires routing setup in your control plane.
[03:33] Maya (Acme): security — we need KMS integration and audit logs. are those available in hosted?
[03:39] Alex (AE): yes, hosted supports envelope encryption and KMS integrations with bring-your-own-key; audit logs and role-based access are available. for the strictest compliance (air-gapped), private on-prem is the path.
[03:50] Samir (SE): quick note on benchmarks — to be meaningful we need representative prompts, a traffic generator with your burst patterns, and realistic context sizes. we'll provide a benchmark harness.
[03:59] Maya (Acme): perfect. timeline: we want a 2-3 week POC, then decision by end of Q4. is that feasible?
[04:06] Alex (AE): yes. recommended approach: start with hosted to validate functional quality and measure latency/cost quickly (1 week). then run targeted dedicated sizing and bring-up if hosted shows variance at peak (another 1-2 weeks). private would be parallel if you require strict network isolation, but that typically takes longer (4-8 weeks depending on procurement).
[04:25] Liam (Infra): procurement risk — if we go private we need SOC2 docs and an order of magnitude estimate for infra specs.
[04:32] Alex (AE): we'll send a security packet and a rough hardware sizing for private. for Dedicated we'll provide a GPU-node recommendation (type + count) based on your qps and seq lengths.
[04:43] Samir (SE): tradeoffs summary: Hosted = fastest, easy logging, pay-as-you-go, good for initial bench; Dedicated = reserved capacity, cheaper unit cost, better tail latency at scale; Private = maximum isolation and control, highest setup lead time and ops burden.
[05:00] Jordan (Product): what about model quantization / multi-tenant models — does Redwood manage quantization?
[05:06] Samir (SE): yes, we have quantization profiles and guidance. runtime supports int8 and mixed precision; we can recommend a quantized variant that trades a little quality for 2-3x throughput improvement. for POC we'll test both FP16 and quantized variants.
[05:20] Maya (Acme): bench details — we need cost per 1k requests and the expected 95th latency at peak. also want model quality checks for personalization — we'll provide NDCG-like metrics.
[05:32] Alex (AE): great. we'll run benchmarks producing token counts, latency (p50/p95), throughput, and cost using your sample prompts and report back.
[05:40] Liam (Infra): networking — if we do hosted, can we VPC connect or do we need dedicated private link?
[05:45] Alex (AE): we support VPC peering and private link options for hosted; Dedicated and Private are more straightforward for private traffic. there might be egress considerations for hosted, we'll include network patterns in the sizing doc.
[05:58] Maya (Acme): any gotchas on KV cache / session caching for personalization?
[06:03] Samir (SE): main considerations: cache hit rates, session token sizes, eviction policies. with our runtime we can pin KV cache for long sessions; for dedicated we can give dedicated cache memory and better cold-start behavior.
[06:17] Jordan (Product): who would run the canary and monitor quality during POC?
[06:21] Alex (AE): Redwood will provide observability dashboards and integrate with your telemetry. we typically set up prometheus/grafana hooks and a quality dashboard for the eval metrics.
[06:31] Maya (Acme): ok, procurement — any long lead times if we pick dedicated?
[06:36] Alex (AE): Dedicated provisioning can take 1-2 weeks after sizing agreement; private can be longer (procurement + infra). hosted is immediate.
[06:44] Liam (Infra): what's the SLA on Dedicated?
[06:47] Alex (AE): we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets on Dedicated; we'll include details in the pricing packet.
[06:53] Samir (SE): one more technical: for re-rank with larger contexts we'll probably use pipeline batching and model variants with truncated contexts to optimize cost. we'll show results in benchmark.
[07:05] Maya (Acme): sounds good. let's recap the success criteria: 95th <200ms for personalization, cost target within 30% of baseline, SOC2 + KMS, residency in us-east.
[07:16] Alex (AE): yep, and actions: we'll send security docs and the benchmark harness; you send prompts and traffic profile. schedule the sizing deep-dive for Dedicated with Samir and Liam.
[07:28] Jordan (Product): agree. any competitors we should be aware of? CTO mentioned OpenAI plus an in-house inference pipeline.
[07:35] Alex (AE): noted. we'll include comparative notes but will focus on measurable benchmarks.
[07:40] Maya (Acme): ok thanks. file an item: we also want RBAC scoped by route, i.e., only product can call model A.
[07:48] Samir (SE): supported — role-based policies by route are available, we'll include example policies.
[07:54] Alex (AE): perfect. i'll follow up with a POC worksheet and timeline. thanks everyone.
[08:00] Meeting ends.

Notes/Artifacts shared in call:
- Link: POC sizing worksheet (redwood.com/poc-sheets/acme) - Alex to populate
- Link: security packet (redwood.com/security/soc2-summary.pdf)
- Benchmark harness repo (github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness)

Transcription notes: occasional word errors (KMS pronounced as K-M-S, KV cache as K-V cache), some overlapping talk at the end.
